slides.say: You wrote use effect. But when does that code actually run? Before the screen updates, or after?

slides.text: React renders, updates the screen, and then runs your Effect.
slides.say: Every time your component renders, React updates the screen first, and then runs the code inside use effect.

slides.text: Runs after the new count is on screen.
slides.say: Here, the heading shows the new count first. Then the effect runs and syncs the browser tab title with it.

slides.text: useEffect "delays" code until that render is reflected on the screen.
slides.say: In other words, use effect delays a piece of code until that render is reflected on the screen.

slides.text: Call it at the top level only. Effects run on the client, never during server rendering.
slides.say: Two rules: call it at the top level of your component, never in loops or conditions. And effects only run on the client, not during server rendering.
Render, update the screen, then run the effect. That is the order.
